tasks.title: Add a read-only stale-session audit command
tasks.acceptance: A read-only command (for example `seshx sessions audit [--repo <path>] [--idle-days N]`) lists every unfinished session with exactly one bucket and the evidence behind it: empty (no commits since start, clean worktree, no checklist), delivered (source commit already reachable from the target branch), unsaved work (uncommitted files or unintegrated commits), corrupt (missing worktree, branch, or pinned coordinator), in lifecycle (ready, lock-waiting, recovery, validation_pending, or promotion_pending), or other; plus idle days since last activity. Output states that liveness is inferred, never proven. It changes no session, Git, or filesystem state, and disposable-repository tests cover each bucket.

tasks.title: Record a last-activity heartbeat on sessions
tasks.acceptance: Lifecycle and `seshx tasks` commands record a session `lastActivityAt` timestamp under the session record lock. Idle calculations use it, falling back to `tasksUpdatedAt`, `startedAt`, and worktree modification time for older records. Older coordinators can still read and resume sessions that carry the new field, and tests cover both new and legacy records.

tasks.title: Add a single-session abandon command
tasks.acceptance: `seshx abandon --session <id> --reason "..."` shows the session's audit bucket, then records a terminal `abandoned` status with the reason and timestamp. It preserves the branch, worktree, commits, and recovery evidence; refuses sessions in lifecycle or recovery state or holding a lock; and requires an explicit flag for sessions with unsaved work. A documented command restores an abandoned session to active. Status and the dashboard show abandoned sessions separately, and they no longer count as unfinished for uninstall or coordinator checks. Disposable-repository tests cover each refusal and the restore path.

tasks.title: Add batch abandon for all matching stale sessions
tasks.acceptance: `seshx abandon --all [--repo <path>] [--idle-days N] [--bucket <list>]` previews matching sessions by default and changes nothing without `--apply`. It selects only the empty, delivered, and corrupt buckets by default; sessions with unsaved work require `--include-unsaved` and are listed individually. Immediately before closing each session it rechecks the session under its record lock and skips any session that changed since the preview or is in lifecycle, lock-waiting, or recovery state. It reports closed and skipped sessions with reasons, preserves all branches, worktrees, commits, and recovery evidence, and tests cover preview, apply, filters, and recheck skips.

tasks.title: Support a central delivery policy, target sync and JSON session output
tasks.acceptance: `seshx begin --policy-file <path>` (else global `deliveryPolicyFile`) strictly validates a `sesh-integrator/delivery-policy@1` file, fails with `policy_missing` or `policy_invalid` before changing anything, resolves the repository rule from the GitHub fetch URL, and records `delivery` with the file's SHA-256 on the session; `integrate` and `resume` use the recorded target and promotion. `begin --sync-target` fast-forwards the local target from its remote under the repository lock with the documented outcomes and never resets or forces. `begin --json` and `status --session <id> --json` print one `sesh-integrator/session-status@1` document, failures print `sesh-integrator/error@1`, and `seshx policy check` validates a file. Tests with disposable repositories cover every sync outcome, policy errors, promotion override and the JSON documents.

tasks.title: Move config history out of the dashboard JSON tab
tasks.acceptance: Dashboard Settings shows config.json history in its own History tab (Global, Repository, JSON, History) instead of under the JSON editor, and a History button in the Settings header opens the same list in a drawer or dialog from any tab. Each entry shows its time and source with Compare with current and Restore. Restore opens the existing Save config.json? confirmation with the diff and saves only after confirmation, without loading the version into the JSON editor or discarding unsaved edits silently. The saved tab choice, keyboard tab navigation, and history-unavailable and empty states keep working, docs/commands.md describes the new placement, and dashboard tests cover the tab, the header button, and restore through confirmation.

tasks.title: Add searchable suggestion fields to dashboard Settings
tasks.acceptance: Dashboard Settings replaces free-text inputs with an accessible, keyboard-operable combobox (type to filter, arrow keys, Enter, Escape) that still accepts typed values: Default target branch lists branches across all registered repositories with how many repositories have each (for example dev — 4 of 5 repos); repository Target branch and Production branch list that repository's branches; Remote lists that repository's git remotes; Reviewers and Assignees are chip inputs suggesting names already used in configuration; Signing program and agent commands suggest detected executables on PATH such as gpg, gpg2 and ssh-keygen. A typed branch that does not exist is offered as Use new branch "<name>", saves only the name, and shows a warning naming the repositories that lack it; saving never creates Git branches. Suggestions come from a read-only dashboard endpoint, the form still works with an empty or failed suggestion list, docs/commands.md describes the fields, and dashboard tests cover filtering, the new-branch option and warning, chip entry and removal, and the suggestion-failure fallback.

tasks.title: Use safe build queue defaults for external users
tasks.acceptance: Machines without an explicit build queue setting default to concurrency auto instead of unlimited, after reviewing why docs/build-queue.md currently restores unlimited; explicit machine settings are preserved and --concurrency unlimited still restores the old behavior. Queue waiting is progress-based by default: the deadline resets whenever a running entry finishes or the waiter moves up, so a busy but moving queue never times out, and --wait-seconds (default 900) limits time without progress rather than total wait. When a running entry's owner is dead, waiters fail promptly instead of waiting out the timeout, with a message naming the entry and the exact seshx queue recover <entry-id> --confirmed-stopped command. seshx queue status shows the effective settings, docs/build-queue.md and docs/configuration.md describe the new defaults and how to restore the old ones, the next release notes call out the default change for existing users, and tests cover the auto default, the deadline reset on progress, the timeout after no progress, and the dead-owner fail-fast.

tasks.title: Let lightweight commands bypass the build queue
tasks.acceptance: A validation tier can mark its commands as lightweight with an explicit, validated configuration option, and those commands run at once without waiting for or using a build queue slot, so a TASKS.json-only change no longer waits minutes behind full test suites for a two-second qtask and prettier check. Repository setup commands can opt in the same way for quick steps such as a warm-cache pnpm install --frozen-lockfile. Tiers and setup commands without the option, mixed changes that select a code tier or the full fallback, and post-integration checks still use the queue. Command output and seshx queue status say when a command bypassed the queue. Invalid option values are rejected, older pinned coordinators that read the same config keep queueing without failing, docs/build-queue.md and docs/configuration.md explain when to use the option and that it is not for builds or test suites, and tests cover a lightweight tier running while the queue is full, a normal tier still waiting, and a mixed change using the queued full fallback.

tasks.title: Keep concurrent full validations reliable and preserve failing test output
tasks.acceptance: On 2026-10-20 five sessions ran full validation at once (before the machine had a queue setting, so concurrency was unlimited); each run took 430-817s instead of the usual 290-320s and corepack pnpm run test exited 1 on every attempt, with no preserved output to tell resource contention from a code defect. Full validation stays reliable when the build queue runs two full validations at once on a 16-core, 11 GB host: vitest worker count is bounded (for example maxWorkers derived from available CPUs divided by the effective queue concurrency, overridable by an environment variable) instead of each run using every core, and the existing 30s test and hook timeouts are reviewed against measured durations under that load. When a validation command fails, the session validationFailure and its incident keep a bounded, secret-redacted tail of that command output plus the path to a full log under the runtime logs directory, so an exit code is never the only evidence. The incident fingerprint includes the failing test names or first error line, not only the command and exit code (fingerprint f40f8da879f4 currently groups 70 unrelated pnpm test failures). The failure record notes the number of running queue entries at failure time so diagnosis can tell resource contention from a code defect. docs/build-queue.md and docs/configuration.md describe the worker bound and override, and tests cover the worker bound, output tail capture and redaction, the fingerprint change, and the queue-load note.
evidence: Tests in test/validation-evidence.test.ts: 'vitest worker bound' (bound formula, queue concurrency, unlimited/invalid queue, SESH_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS override, repository vitest config), 'failure output evidence' (redaction, bounded tail, failing-test and first-error extraction, record tail/log/queue load with a second running entry, never-run command), 'incident fingerprint' (separation, normalization, unchanged legacy fingerprints), and 'validation failure through the CLI' (session, incident and status evidence without secrets).

Timeout review 2026-10-20: two full suites through the build queue at concurrency 2 (7 Vitest workers each) on the 16-thread, 11 GB WSL host passed 494 tests in 352 s and 358 s; slowest test 18.0 s including hooks, next 13.7 s, so the 30 s test and hook timeouts were kept.

tasks.title: Batch concurrent integrations into one validated merge
tasks.acceptance: Integration validation runs while the per-repository lock is held (mergeAndValidate in src/handoff.ts), so sessions that finish together are validated one at a time: a full integration validation took about 290-320s on 2026-10-20, so the Nth waiting session waits roughly N x 5 minutes and the 4th or later can exceed the default 900s lockWaitSeconds. When two or more sessions for the same repository are waiting to integrate, the next lock holder merges every waiting session's exact readyCommit into one integration candidate in a deterministic order, runs the strictest integration validation any member selected (the full fallback for any code change) once on the combined tree, and promotes it with the existing expected-previous-target check. Each member session records the shared staging and promoted commits with its own completion summary, rollout classification and follow-ups, and a waiting integrate process whose session was promoted in a batch exits with that session's completion summary instead of integrating again. A member whose merge conflicts is left out of the batch and integrated alone through the existing conflict-resume flow. When batch validation fails, the tool isolates the failing member (for example by validating halves) so passing members still promote and only the failing one becomes validation_pending; no session is promoted on a tree that was not validated. Batch size has a configurable cap, batching can be disabled per repository, older pinned coordinators keep integrating one session at a time without failing, and lock-wait output names the batch a waiting session joined. docs/configuration.md and README's How work comes together section describe batching, and disposable-repository tests cover a three-session batch, a conflicting member, a failing member isolated from passing ones, the cap, and batching disabled.

tasks.title: Reuse source validation when the target moved only by lightweight-tier changes
tasks.acceptance: Integration already reuses source validation results when the merged tree matches the validated source tree (session_mvh2l5y8_fa64bc2695 on 2026-10-20 reran only build, with 2.8s of integration validation), but any target movement changes the tree and reruns the whole plan: four sessions integrated on 2026-10-20 after the target moved and each reran format:check, typecheck, test and build. When every path that differs between the validated source tree and the merged integration tree matches one configured validation tier that opts in (for example task-register or docs, so the target moved only by such commits), integration runs that tier's integration commands on the merged tree, reuses the source results for the other commands, and still runs integration-only commands such as build. A differing path outside that tier, a tier without the opt-in, recovery reconciliation (recoveryPhase local_target), or validationCache off keeps the current full rerun. The opt-in is an explicit per-tier option that is validated, rejected when invalid, and ignored by older pinned coordinators without failing. Integration output and performance metrics say which commands were reused and why. docs/configuration.md explains that the opt-in asserts the tier's paths cannot change other checks' results, and disposable-repository tests cover a TASKS.json-only target movement reusing results, a code movement rerunning everything, a mixed movement rerunning everything, and a tier without the opt-in.

tasks.title: Detect the harness automatically when begin omits --harness
tasks.acceptance: seshx begin without --harness currently records codex for compatibility, so Claude Code sessions begun with a plain begin --create-worktree before 2026-10-08 (for example session_mu7grty6_d5d7b75f64) are labeled codex, and nested conflict resolution and incident diagnosis use the wrong harness. When --harness is omitted, begin detects the harness for every supported harness (codex, claude, antigravity, grok): first from a documented environment marker (Claude Code sets CLAUDECODE=1; Codex, Antigravity and Grok markers are verified by running env inside each harness before use, and CODEX_SANDBOX alone is not treated as reliable), then from the parent process chain (claude, codex, antigravity/agy, grok). If nothing is detected, begin fails with a message asking for --harness instead of silently recording codex. An explicit --harness that contradicts a detected harness prints a warning and keeps the explicit value. begin output and status show the recorded harness and whether it was explicit or detected. Existing session records are not rewritten. docs/harnesses.md and docs/commands.md describe the detection order and markers, and tests cover detection for each harness by environment and by process ancestry, the undetected failure, and the mismatch warning.

tasks.title: Keep validation cache hits when the shell environment changes between commands
tasks.acceptance: validationFingerprint in src/cache.ts hashes the entire process environment (validationEnvironment, minus PWD and OLDPWD), so any per-shell variable change between seshx validate and seshx integrate misses the cache. Agents run eval "$(fnm env)" before each command, and every call creates a new FNM_MULTISHELL_PATH directory (for example /run/user/1000/fnm_multishells/<pid>_<timestamp>) that is also added to PATH. On 2026-10-21 session_mviogb9q_8e23fb70b0 (agent-delly) integrated with integrationSourceReuse exact-tree, meaning the merged tree was the validated source tree, yet had 0 cache hits and reran build, typecheck and test for 436s. The next waiting session, session_mviogryh_f312d80dfa, waited 442s on the lock behind it. session_mviogkxo_1a93d7d626 also got 0 cache hits on its third validate of the same tree. The validation cache key stays the same across shells with the same effective toolchain: volatile per-shell values (FNM_MULTISHELL_PATH, fnm_multishells PATH entries, and similar documented per-shell variables such as SHLVL and _) are excluded or normalized, while changes that can alter results (resolved node and pnpm versions, NODE_OPTIONS, CI, other result-affecting variables or an explicit allowlist) still miss. Values are never persisted. docs/configuration.md describes what the key includes. Tests cover a validate then integrate under different fnm multishell paths reusing results, a changed Node version or NODE_OPTIONS still rerunning, and older cache entries treated as misses without failing.

tasks.title: Tell agents to run long validate and integrate commands in the background, not under a timeout
tasks.acceptance: On 2026-10-21 session_mviogkxo_1a93d7d626 (Claude Code, agent-delly) ran timeout 590 seshx validate in the foreground to stay under the harness's 10-minute command limit. The full validation was killed at 593s and recorded only "Build queue cancelled; no successful result recorded." (incident at 2026-10-21T22:52:41Z), and the next full run started from scratch. The bundled skill (skill/sesh-integrator-workflow/SKILL.md) and the managed global guidance (GLOBAL_AGENTS_SNIPPET.md) tell agents to run validate, integrate and resume through the harness's background or long-running execution with its completion notification, never to wrap them in timeout or a foreground limit shorter than the configured build-queue wait, and to wait with the harness's bounded wait rather than polling. When validate, integrate or resume is stopped by a signal, the failure message and incident name the signal and elapsed time and say to rerun in the background, instead of only saying the build queue was cancelled. Tests cover the signal message, and the installed guidance check passes after install.

tasks.title: Finish local-target recovery when another session moved staging during conflict resolution
tasks.acceptance: Local-target recovery (reconcileLocalTarget in src/handoff.ts) saves the staging commit as stagingBefore when it starts, then advances staging with git update-ref against that saved value: once after committing the resolved result and again on resume when resultCommit is already recorded. Other sessions keep integrating while a recovery waits for its conflict fix, so the saved value goes stale and the update is always refused. Resume repeats the same update, so the session can never finish. On 2026-10-24 agent-delly session_mvluq35m_47d7a85ab8 (PC-042) started recovery at staging 21260c1 and committed result 33f2a63 at 04:49Z. session_mvlwyn6l_5acdbaf30d had already moved staging to 22e8fb6 at 04:46Z, and that commit already contained both 21260c1 and the target 24d0f18. The update was refused (incident CH-20261024-B42D42) and the session was left in needs_review, although its work was already on dev. abandon refuses needs_review sessions, so there was no supported way to close it. Before advancing staging, recovery re-reads it instead of trusting stagingBefore. If staging is unchanged, it proceeds as today. If the session's staging integration commit is already on the target branch, it records the session as integrated through that promotion, closes the recovery bundle and keeps the stale result in localTargetRecoveryHistory without creating a commit. If staging moved forward and still contains stagingBefore, it moves the stale result to history and restarts reconciliation from the new staging with full revalidation. If staging diverged, it stops with needs_review and a message that names the commits, as today. Integration tests with disposable repositories cover all three cases, with a second session integrating while the first waits on a local-target conflict. Afterwards, resume session_mvluq35m_47d7a85ab8 with a coordinator that includes the fix (resume records it as recoveryCoordinator) and confirm that it finishes.
